readiness.mainReason: The deck presents findings but never says which service to launch first, so it does not answer the client's question.
readiness.highestRiskIssue: Slide 9 concludes only that further analysis may be useful and makes no recommendation.
readiness.whatCouldChangeIt: A clear recommendation drawn from the demand evidence would move this toward targeted revision.

strengths.point: The evidence gathering is honest and multi-source for an early draft, which gives the team a real basis to decide from.
strengths.quote: We interviewed staff, surveyed 120 patients and reviewed local health data.

findings.title: The deck answers none of the client's question: which service to launch first.
findings.principle: Governing insight: a deck must state its one answer.
findings.diagnosis: The client asked which of three services to launch first under one-service capacity. Slide 9 lists considerations and defers to further analysis. No option is chosen.
findings.why: The client commissioned a decision and received a summary of options. They cannot act on considerations.
findings.reflect: Given your own evidence, which service would you launch first and what is the one reason.
findings.fix: State the recommendation up front and let the findings defend it. Your evidence already leans one way, so commit to it and show the reasoning.

findings.title: The demand evidence points toward one service but the deck stops at description.
findings.principle: Analysis over description: state the implication of each finding.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 8 shows mental health is the top unmet need and slide 5 shows matching demand. The deck reports this and moves on without drawing the implication for the decision.

evidence.quote: 40% of surveyed patients said mental health was their top unmet need, 30% said diabetes, 20% physiotherapy, 10% other.
Patients report long waits for mental-health support elsewhere. Staff see demand.

findings.why: The interpretation is the value the client is paying for. The raw facts they could gather themselves.
findings.reflect: What does the 40% top-need figure, read with the demand signal, imply for which service to launch first.
findings.fix: For each finding add its so-what, then connect the so-whats to a single recommendation.

findings.title: The titles are labels, so the argument cannot be read from them.
findings.principle: Action titles: titles carry the message.
findings.diagnosis: Titles such as Agenda, Background and Considerations name topics not conclusions. A reader skimming the titles learns nothing about the answer.
findings.why: A busy client or funder reads the titles first. Labels waste that read.
findings.reflect: If a reader saw only your titles, what would they learn about your recommendation.
findings.fix: Once you have chosen the recommendation, rewrite each content title as a full-sentence assertion that supports it.

comments.problem: "capacity to add one new service" is not quantified in staff hours or budget.
comments.why: The launch decision depends on what running one service actually costs.
comments.fix: State the capacity envelope so the options can be compared against it.

questionsForLead: Did the team reach a recommendation and leave it out, or not reach one at all.
Does the survey sample of 120 represent Client C's patient mix.
What does 'capacity to add one new service' mean in staff and budget terms.
Were staff asked which service they could deliver well, not only which has demand.

learningNote.lesson: Findings are not a deliverable. The client is paying for the judgment that turns findings into a decision.
learningNote.weakHabit: Stopping at 'here is what we found' instead of 'here is what you should do'.
learningNote.exercise: Write the one-sentence recommendation first, then check each slide earns its place by supporting it. Cut the slides that do not.

notAssessed: Whether mental health is genuinely the right launch given clinical and staffing factors the deck does not cover.
The accuracy of the local health data and the survey. Sources are named but not provided.
Visual design and layout. Only slide text was provided.
Client C's real capacity and budget. Not quantified in the deck.
